# T2.04: the MMU fault

The fault (T2.03) was the engine reading past the end of the input picture. Adding unmapped-free slack after the
picture (`NVENC_VAR=inpad=<KB>`) removes it:

| 256x128 input (0xc000 bytes) + pad | result |
|---|---|
| 0 | FAULT_PTE at input + 0xc000 |
| 4 KB, 8 KB | FAULT_PTE at input + 0xe000 |
| 12 KB, 16 KB, 64 KB, 1 MB | no fault |

So at 256x128 the engine touches 8-12 KB past the chroma plane (32-48 chroma rows' worth at pitch 256). 256x64 faults
at its end too (input + 0x6000). Larger sizes (256x256, 512x256, 1920x1088) didn't fault even without the pad, but
there the next VA range happens to be mapped, so that proves nothing. Why the engine reads that far is not known
yet. It could be read-ahead, a chroma height rounding we don't match, or the engine stopping early because of the
error below. T2.08 (input layout) will look at it again.

Change: `encode1` now allocates 64 KB of slack after the input picture by default (`inpad`, KB).

With the fault gone the engine runs further. It writes the status buffer (`pic_type 3`, `error_status 1`,
`ucode_error_status 0`, no bits), and the error notifier now reports info32 `0x2f` = 47 =
`ROBUST_CHANNEL_NVENC0_ERROR` instead of an MMU fault. The semaphore isn't released. That's T2.05 (task text
updated: T2.04 is "no MMU fault", T2.05 is the engine error).
